step2_answer: No. The BMRDA Act does not require BMRDA to prepare its plans with the city government (ULG). It does not require the city government to approve, agree to or jointly prepare the plan. It does not require BMRDA to consult the city government, or say that BMRDA "may" do so. The Act's other links to local bodies run the other way. BMRDA may hand plans to a local authority to carry out (s.9(1)(viii)). It can give directions that local bodies must follow (s.18). Section 31 adds Section 81-C to the Karnataka Town and Country Planning (T&CP) Act. Under 81-C, Planning Authorities in the region send their outline and comprehensive development plans to the State Government through BMRDA, which acts as Director of Town Planning for them. This makes BMRDA a reviewer of local plans; it gives local bodies no role in BMRDA's own plans. The Mayor of the old Bangalore city corporation sits on the Authority (s.3(3)(d)). That is board membership, not a required consultation on plans. Under the BMRDA Act alone, this is the 0 band ("no formal role"). The T&CP Act's own text is not in the Citation Sheet, so the score is provisional.
